text:
Ian Cole is 37, on his tenth NHL team, and still playing 19 minutes a night, more than 20 lately. He passed 1,000 career games this season, a two-time Stanley Cup winner with Pittsburgh still doing the hard work on a young Blackhawks blue line.

The points barely exist: his first assist came on Nov 17 against Toronto, per CBS Sports. That's not his job. Evolving-Hockey had him 36th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, taking chances away at the 93rd percentile, though his results ran ahead of the chances.

This season Chicago gets 45% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about four points better than without him. On a team that struggles to control play, he's part of the solution.

The skating is the limitation: NHL Edge has his speed and acceleration near the bottom of the league, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged exits as a weak spot (22% with possession). What to watch: how long the Blackhawks keep leaning on him this hard. The minutes are rising, not falling.
